title: Neurogliaform Cells
intro: Neurogliaform cells are small interneurons with an extraordinarily dense, fine axon. Instead of making ordinary one-to-one synapses they release GABA into the space around them, a form of volume transmission that inhibits every nearby cell through slow GABA-B as well as GABA-A receptors. They are abundant in layer 1, where they inhibit the apical tufts of pyramidal cells, and they are one of the few interneuron types found in every cortical area and in the hippocampus.

items: Morphology: a small round soma with short, many-branched dendrites and an axon that forms a dense cloud of thin branches, often wider than the dendrites, with many boutons that do not face a postsynaptic partner.

Molecular identity: most belong to the 5HT3aR family; in mouse many express neuron-derived neurotrophic factor (NDNF) in layer 1, or reelin and neuropeptide Y; they are the main layer 1 interneuron type along with a VIP-like 'single bouquet' type.

Firing: late spiking. A ramp-like delay of hundreds of milliseconds before the first spike at threshold current, from a slowly inactivating A-type potassium current; then regular firing with little adaptation.

Output: GABA release that spills over to extrasynaptic receptors, giving slow GABA-A currents (decay of tens of ms) and GABA-B currents (rise and decay over hundreds of ms) in nearly all cells within the axon cloud (Tamas et al. 2003; Olah et al. 2009). Many neurogliaform cells are also electrically coupled to each other and to other interneurons.

Inputs: in layer 1, long-range cortical feedback and higher-order thalamus, as well as cholinergic input; they are therefore positioned to inhibit the same tufts that feedback excites (Abs et al. 2018; Cohen-Kashi Malina et al. 2021).

Slow, widespread suppression: neurogliaform inhibition lasts long enough to suppress dendritic calcium spikes and NMDA plateaus for hundreds of milliseconds, setting the overall gain of top-down input (Palmer et al. 2012 showed that inhibition of layer 5 dendritic calcium spikes from the opposite hemisphere runs through layer 1 interneurons and GABA-B receptors).
Feedforward inhibition of feedback: feedback that excites tufts also excites layer 1 neurogliaform cells, which then dampen the tufts, a self-limiting loop.
Learning: NDNF-positive layer 1 cells in auditory cortex respond to aversive stimuli and gate associative learning by controlling tuft excitability (Abs et al. 2018).
Blue Brain's NGC m-types (NGC-DA, NGC-SA) in layer 1 and the other layers, with continuous non-accommodating and delayed e-types.
Point neurons with a delayed first spike (an A-current, or an adaptive threshold that starts high) reproduce late spiking; the Allen GLIF models fitted to Ndnf and Lamp5 cells capture the slow onset.

Volume transmission is modelled as a slow, non-specific inhibitory synapse from each neurogliaform cell onto all cells within a radius, with a GABA-B kinetic scheme (Destexhe, Mainen & Sejnowski 1998 give standard GABA-B kinetics with G-protein activation).

blocks.text: What this means for your SNN

items: If you have apical compartments and feedback input, a slow, non-selective inhibitory population on those compartments keeps feedback from saturating them.
Model their output as a slow GABA-B-like conductance (time constants of 50 to 300 ms) onto every apical compartment nearby, rather than as fast, sparse synapses.
For a first model they can be folded into a slow, global inhibition term on the apical input.
